data.cultural_impact: The name "Paulianne" pays tribute to the profound influence of St. Paul in Christian history. His letters to the early Christian communities have formed the backbone of Christian doctrine and piety. Paulianne may inspire thoughts of humility, dedication, and spiritual strength, much like the man himself.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Paulianne is a constant reminder of the importance of humility in the Christian faith. Humility signifies a submission to God’s will, acknowledging that God is the true source of all wisdom, strength, and guidance. In naming a child Paulianne, one may hope for her to embody the virtues of a humble and devoted follower of Christ. Moreover, Paulianne is an embodiment of the grace, wisdom, and strength that St. Paul demonstrated throughout his teachings and missionary journeys.

historical_references.reference: Paulianne, a Christian martyr and virgin, was venerated in the diocese of Tours, France. Her feast day was celebrated on April 21. She is believed to have been a slave, and was martyred during the persecutions under Diocletian in the late 3rd century AD.

Paulianne was a noblewoman in the city of Chartres, France, who dedicated her life to prayer and charitable acts during the 11th century AD. She became known as the 'Lady of Charity' and was canonized by the Catholic Church in the 13th century.
